reason: Stagehand's driver half (navigate, tabs, screenshot) is provided by a compiled-in, Node-free CDP provider built on chromedp; its AI half (act, observe, extract), which calls a second model outside the session log, usage accounting and cancellation, is not kept and is replaced by a page description plus plain input actions used by the session's own model.

Upstream uses this package only to locate an installed stable Chrome, start it and read its DevTools address (launch.ts:6, :26, :40, :54); it never downloads a browser. In Go the lookup is a table of install paths and the start goes through the harness's single spawn helper, with a pipe transport so no address needs to be read.

The npm package is a Node addon loaded into the host process; a Go binary cannot load it, and linking the same native code would need cgo and would keep third-party native code and the launching terminal's desktop permission inside the host. The in-process provider is folded into the external Cua Driver provider, which starts the operator-installed cua-driver program over MCP and exposes the same tool catalogue.

Playwright is upstream's test-only driver for 249 browser test files. With server-rendered HTML most of those checks need no browser; the remaining real-browser scenarios are Go tests on chromedp, the module the product already uses, so the test lane needs no Node, no driver download and no browser cache. Firefox and Safari runs use a second back end of the same scenario helper that speaks W3C WebDriver with net/http (DH-ADR-PLAYWRIGHT-2), because the product's only UI client is the user's own browser (DH-ADR-18).

These scripts build, sign, notarize, verify and stage the macOS computer-use helper application and reuse earlier signed artifacts. The owner decided that the Go project ships no native helper and that computer use works only through an external MCP server the operator installs, so there is no helper to build, sign, verify or stage and the release tooling is not ported.

The exemption exists because only this Stagehand release matches the workspace's reviewed zod version, which the provider must pin because it passes schema objects into the SDK. The Go design has no Stagehand dependency and passes no schema object to a third-party library, so the coupling and the exemption disappear.

The exemption lets a reviewed native runtime be installed with the harness before the installer's waiting period ends. No Cua Driver code is installed with or loaded into the Go harness; the driver is a program the operator installs and its version is recorded at connection.

title: The native Cua Driver runtime shares the host process: a native crash ends every session and desktop permission belongs to the launching application

reason: Code that reads or controls the desktop runs only in a separate process, so a crash fails pending calls and not the host, and the operating-system permission belongs to that program's own identity.
